symptom: PC1 in VLAN 10 (Fa0/2) cannot ping PC2 also in VLAN 10 (Fa0/4) on the same switch.
topology_note: SW1 access switch, single VLAN 10 segment, no trunk involved. PC1=192.168.10.11/24, PC2=192.168.10.12/24.
show_output:
show vlan brief
VLAN10  users  active  Fa0/2
(Fa0/4 not listed under VLAN10; shows under VLAN1)
show interfaces status
Fa0/4  connected  1  a-full  a-100  10/100BaseTX
expected_fault: Fa0/4 was never assigned to VLAN 10 (still default VLAN 1) so PC2 is on a different broadcast domain than PC1.

symptom: All PCs on VLAN 20 lost connectivity to each other after a trunk link was reconfigured.
topology_note: SW1-SW2 trunk on Gi0/1. VLAN 20 exists on both switches.
show_output:
show interfaces trunk
Port  Vlans allowed on trunk
Gi0/1  1,10,30
(VLAN 20 missing from allowed list)
expected_fault: VLAN 20 was pruned/removed from the trunk's allowed-VLAN list, isolating VLAN 20 traffic across the trunk.

symptom: New PC plugged into Fa0/10 gets no link light activity reflected in switch status and cannot get an IP.
topology_note: Fa0/10 was previously used for a printer and administratively shut down after removal.
show_output:
show interfaces Fa0/10
FastEthernet0/10 is administratively down, line protocol is down
expected_fault: Port Fa0/10 is administratively shut down; needs 'no shutdown'.

symptom: PC in VLAN 30 can ping its own gateway but not other hosts in VLAN 30 on a different access switch.
topology_note: Two access switches connected via a link configured as access mode instead of trunk.
show_output:
show interfaces Gi0/2 switchport
Administrative Mode: static access
Operational Mode: static access
Access Mode VLAN: 1
expected_fault: Inter-switch link is set to access mode on VLAN 1 instead of trunk, so VLAN 30 traffic cannot cross between switches.

symptom: PC gets a valid IP via DHCP but cannot reach anything outside its own subnet, including the gateway.
show_output:
show ip interface brief (PC ipconfig)
IPv4 Address: 192.168.5.20
Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.0
Default Gateway: 192.168.6.1
expected_fault: Default gateway on the PC (192.168.6.1) does not match the router's actual interface IP (192.168.5.1) — wrong gateway configured, likely bad DHCP pool default-router entry.

symptom: PC can ping its configured gateway IP but the router shows the interface as down.
topology_note: PC statically configured, router Gi0/1 connects to the access switch.
show_output:
show ip interface brief
GigabitEthernet0/1  192.168.7.1  YES manual  administratively down  down
expected_fault: Router interface Gi0/1 is administratively shut down; the PC's ping to gateway is actually failing (symptom mis-stated) or ARP is being answered by another device — root cause is the shut interface needing 'no shutdown'.

symptom: PC can ping the gateway but not a server one hop further away, even though the server is up.
topology_note: Router has two interfaces, one to the PC subnet, one to the server subnet.
show_output:
show ip route
C  192.168.8.0/24 is directly connected, Gi0/0
(no route for 192.168.9.0/24 present)
expected_fault: Router is missing a route/connected entry for the server's subnet (192.168.9.0/24) — likely the far interface is down or not configured with an IP.

symptom: PC gets IP via DHCP but the gateway field is blank, so PC can only reach local subnet.
topology_note: DHCP pool configured on router.
show_output:
show running-config | section dhcp
ip dhcp pool LAN1
 network 192.168.10.0 255.255.255.0
(no 'default-router' line present)
expected_fault: DHCP pool is missing the 'default-router' statement, so clients never receive a gateway address.

symptom: PC shows a 169.254.x.x address instead of an address from the expected pool.
topology_note: DHCP server is a router with pool 192.168.11.0/24, PC on same VLAN.
show_output:
show ip dhcp binding
(no bindings listed)
show interfaces Gi0/0
GigabitEthernet0/0 is up, line protocol is down (disabled)
expected_fault: Line protocol down on the router's LAN interface prevents DHCPDISCOVER from reaching the server, so the PC self-assigns an APIPA address.

symptom: Two PCs on the same VLAN intermittently lose connectivity and event logs show duplicate IP warnings.
topology_note: One PC static, one PC DHCP, same subnet.
show_output:
show ip dhcp conflict
IP address       Detection method   Detection time
192.168.12.15    Gratuitous ARP     *10:15:03 UTC
expected_fault: A statically configured PC is using an address inside the DHCP pool range, causing a duplicate IP conflict with a DHCP client.

symptom: PCs on VLAN 40 do not receive DHCP addresses while PCs on VLAN 10 (same router) work fine.
topology_note: Router-on-a-stick with subinterfaces per VLAN.
show_output:
show running-config | section dhcp
ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.40.1 192.168.40.254
ip dhcp pool VLAN40
 network 192.168.40.0 255.255.255.0
expected_fault: The excluded-address range accidentally covers the entire pool (1-254), leaving no addresses available to lease.

symptom: Remote VLAN's PCs get no IP; DHCP server is centralized on another subnet via a router.
topology_note: Router acts as relay between VLAN 50 and the DHCP server subnet.
show_output:
show running-config interface Gi0/0.50
interface GigabitEthernet0/0.50
 encapsulation dot1Q 50
 ip address 192.168.50.1 255.255.255.0
(no 'ip helper-address' line)
expected_fault: Missing 'ip helper-address' on the VLAN 50 subinterface, so DHCP broadcasts never get relayed to the remote DHCP server.

symptom: PC can ping the server by IP address but 'ping server1.local' fails with unknown host.
topology_note: PC configured via DHCP, DNS server IP included in pool.
show_output:
ipconfig /all
DNS Servers: 0.0.0.0
expected_fault: DHCP pool is not distributing a valid DNS server address ('dns-server' statement missing or wrong), so name resolution fails while raw connectivity works.

symptom: Name resolution works for internal server names but not for the intended web server hostname.
topology_note: Simple internal DNS server configured with static records.
show_output:
show running-config (DNS host entries)
ip host server1 192.168.20.10
ip host fileserver 192.168.20.11
(no entry for 'webserver')
expected_fault: No static host entry exists for 'webserver' on the DNS/router host table, so that specific name cannot resolve while others do.

symptom: All PCs on the network report slow or failed DNS lookups, though the DNS server itself pings fine.
topology_note: DNS server is a router configured with 'ip dns server' and host entries.
show_output:
show running-config | include dns
(no 'ip dns server' line present)
expected_fault: The router's DNS proxy service ('ip dns server') was never enabled, so it never answers DNS queries even though the host table exists.

symptom: PC in VLAN 10 can reach VLAN 20 but not the remote branch subnet across a WAN link.
topology_note: Two routers connected via serial link, static routing used.
show_output:
show ip route
S  192.168.30.0/24 [1/0] via 10.0.0.2
(missing route back: no entry for 192.168.10.0/24 on Router2)
expected_fault: Router2 is missing a static (or return) route back to 192.168.10.0/24, so replies from the branch never make it home — asymmetric routing failure.

symptom: OSPF neighbors never form between two routers on a shared segment.
topology_note: Both routers configured for OSPF area 0 on the connecting link.
show_output:
show ip ospf interface brief
R1: Gi0/0  area 0  Hello 10  Dead 40
R2: Gi0/0  area 0  Hello 5   Dead 20
expected_fault: Mismatched OSPF hello/dead timers between the two routers prevent neighbor adjacency from forming.

symptom: Static route was added for a remote subnet but traffic still fails to reach it.
topology_note: Static route entered pointing to an interface that is not the correct next hop.
show_output:
show running-config | include ip route
ip route 192.168.40.0 255.255.255.0 192.168.1.1
show ip route
S  192.168.40.0/24 [1/0] via 192.168.1.1, but 192.168.1.1 is unreachable (not directly connected)
expected_fault: The static route's next-hop IP (192.168.1.1) is not reachable/directly connected from this router, so the route is effectively unusable.

symptom: Inter-VLAN routing fails for a newly added VLAN even though the router-on-a-stick already routes other VLANs fine.
topology_note: Router Gi0/0 has subinterfaces for VLAN 10, 20, and the new VLAN 60.
show_output:
show running-config interface Gi0/0.60
interface GigabitEthernet0/0.60
 encapsulation dot1Q 60
(no ip address configured)
expected_fault: Subinterface for VLAN 60 has no IP address configured, so the router cannot route for that VLAN.

symptom: PC gets IP and can ping its gateway in VLAN 30, but cannot reach the server in VLAN 10 across the router.
topology_note: Router-on-a-stick between VLAN 10 (server) and VLAN 30 (PC); an ACL was recently applied inbound on the VLAN 30 subinterface.
show_output:
show access-lists
Extended IP access list BLOCK_30
 10 deny ip 192.168.30.0 0.0.0.255 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255
 20 permit ip any any
show ip interface Gi0/0.30
 Inbound access list is BLOCK_30
expected_fault: ACL 'BLOCK_30' explicitly denies VLAN 30 -> VLAN 10 traffic before the permit-any line, blocking the PC from reaching the server. Layer 3/4 issue, matches the worked example in the brief.

symptom: Telnet to the router management IP fails from an admin PC, but ping to the same IP succeeds.
topology_note: VTY lines protected by an access-class ACL.
show_output:
show running-config | section line vty
line vty 0 4
 access-class ADMIN_ONLY in
show access-lists ADMIN_ONLY
 10 permit host 192.168.1.50
expected_fault: access-class ACL only permits host 192.168.1.50; the admin PC's actual address is not in the permitted list, so Telnet (Layer 4/7) is blocked while ICMP (which isn't filtered by access-class) still passes.

symptom: Web traffic (HTTP) from PCs is blocked but all other traffic to the same server works fine.
topology_note: Extended ACL applied outbound on server-facing interface.
show_output:
show access-lists
Extended IP access list WEB_FILTER
 10 deny tcp any any eq 80
 20 permit ip any any
expected_fault: ACL explicitly denies TCP port 80 (HTTP) before the general permit statement, blocking only web traffic — Layer 4 port-specific filtering.

symptom: An ACL meant to block only one host is blocking an entire subnet instead.
topology_note: Standard ACL applied to restrict a single problem PC.
show_output:
show access-lists
Standard IP access list RESTRICT
 10 deny 192.168.15.0 0.0.0.255
 20 permit any
expected_fault: Wildcard mask (0.0.0.255) matches the entire /24 subnet instead of a single host (should be 0.0.0.0 with a host statement), over-blocking the range.

symptom: Internal PCs can ping each other but cannot reach the internet-simulated outside server.
topology_note: Router configured with NAT overload (PAT) for internet access.
show_output:
show ip nat translations
(no entries)
show running-config | include ip nat
ip nat inside source list 1 interface Gi0/1 overload
(interface Gi0/0 missing 'ip nat inside')
expected_fault: Inside interface (Gi0/0, facing the LAN) is missing the 'ip nat inside' command, so no traffic is being matched for translation.

symptom: Only some internal PCs can reach the outside server; others time out.
topology_note: NAT uses access-list 1 to define which inside sources are translated.
show_output:
show access-lists 1
Standard IP access list 1
 10 permit 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.127
expected_fault: NAT access-list 1 wildcard mask only covers the first half of the subnet (0.0.0.127), so PCs in the upper half (.128-.254) are never translated.

symptom: Outside host cannot initiate a connection to an internal server that should be reachable via port forwarding.
topology_note: Static NAT/PAT entry intended for a web server on 192.168.1.100.
show_output:
show running-config | include ip nat inside source
(no static or port-forward entry present, only 'overload' dynamic PAT configured)
expected_fault: No static NAT / port-forwarding rule exists for the internal web server, so unsolicited inbound connections have nothing to map to and are dropped.

symptom: NAT overload was configured correctly, but the outside interface never shows as such.
topology_note: Router has two interfaces; NAT commands were applied but one directional keyword was set wrong.
show_output:
show ip nat statistics
Total active translations: 0
Outside interfaces:
 Inside interfaces:
 Gi0/0
 Gi0/1
expected_fault: Both interfaces were configured as 'ip nat inside' — no interface was marked 'ip nat outside', so NAT has no outside interface to translate toward.

symptom: Guest Wi-Fi laptop can reach the internal file server, which should be isolated from guests.
topology_note: Guest WLAN mapped to VLAN 99; internal servers in VLAN 10. Matches the guest isolation example in the brief.
show_output:
show vlan brief
VLAN99  Guest  active  Gi0/2
show access-lists
(no ACL applied to Gi0/0.99 subinterface)
expected_fault: Guest VLAN 99 has no isolation ACL applied on its routed subinterface, so it is not actually segmented from VLAN 10 — a security/isolation failure, not a connectivity bug.

symptom: Wireless clients can associate with the SSID but never get an IP address.
topology_note: WLC/AP bridges wireless clients onto VLAN 25, DHCP relay expected via router.
show_output:
show running-config interface Gi0/0.25
interface GigabitEthernet0/0.25
 encapsulation dot1Q 25
 ip address 192.168.25.1 255.255.255.0
(no ip helper-address, and no local dhcp pool for VLAN25)
expected_fault: VLAN 25 has neither a local DHCP pool nor an 'ip helper-address' pointing to a DHCP server, so associated wireless clients never receive an address.

symptom: Wireless clients repeatedly fail to associate with the configured SSID at all (no IP issue, association itself fails).
topology_note: AP configured with WPA2-PSK; students entered the passphrase on clients.
show_output:
AP running-config (Packet Tracer GUI)
SSID: LabWiFi
Authentication: WPA2-PSK
Passphrase: Cisco12345
(client device shows passphrase: Cisco123)
expected_fault: Passphrase mismatch between the AP (Cisco12345) and the client configuration (Cisco123) causes authentication/association failure at Layer 2, before any IP addressing is relevant.
